summary.prose: Start a review from the submitted change set, inspect its committed source and tests one task at a time, and save each completed assessment in one JSON file. Keep daemon and controller reviewer behavior aligned while preserving their different disconnect lifetimes. Publish a versioned task-based CR without invoking the old dimension/chunk review engine.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary:
Use one task-oriented review coordinator over the existing provider, task and artifact infrastructure. The model reads a task's functional summary, committed Story/LLD/Plan references, selected changed segments and complete test details, investigates as needed, then returns ordinary findings and a task result. The host handles identities, ordering, timing, JSON persistence and CR publication. No model-facing evidence aliases, coverage ledgers, qualification probes, signing keys, new artifact types or multi-round dimension/chunk engine are introduced. Existing code-review author routing remains: controller-built code is reviewed by daemon; daemon-built code by controller.

Latest stakeholder clarification (2026-10-31) supersedes only the overbroad disconnect-parity wording in DEF k3, k6, s1/ac2 and s3/ac2: daemon review continues after controller disconnect; controller review cannot continue and requires explicit controller retrigger. Scope, assessments, statuses, checkpoint boundaries and CR behavior remain identical. No background CLI is relabelled as the controller party. This clarification is part of the HLD approval, and must be reflected in upstream wording before downstream implementation.

Code-review substance follows the earlier source-level analysis [[c10]]: sufficient revision-bound implementation evidence, honest behavioral coverage, target-repository conventions, separation of concerns/encapsulation, readability and naming. Optional framework or style advice is not a blocking defect. Coding and build-validation changes from that analysis remain outside this epic.

ownedContracts.name: Committed review packet and task assessment
ownedContracts.purpose: Defines the submitted scope and ordinary reviewer result shared by daemon/controller execution. Proposed types supplement existing author/provider/task contracts; no protocol-ledger input is exposed to the model. Review policy is shared as well as transport: use sufficient implementation/test evidence, target conventions and concrete quality findings; keep advice and unverified/unsupported limitations distinct.

ownedContracts.name: Single checkpoint file and execution lifecycle
ownedContracts.purpose: One host-owned JSON contains all attempts. Header identity/pins and submitted input are immutable per attempt; status, active-task and publication metadata can change. Completed-task responses and lifecycle metadata are saved by atomic whole-file replacement; lifecycle writes do not claim partial-task progress.

ownedContracts.name: Permanent CR projection and story cleanup
ownedContracts.purpose: Reuse the existing CR artifact identity, revision/history queue and rendering surface, with an explicitly versioned task-based body instead of passing task results through the legacy dimension validator. Version-1 records remain readable and use their existing validator. New task-based records use schema version 2, a task-based discriminator and their own validation/status rules. Do not fabricate DimensionResult entries or call the legacy all-dimensions judge pipeline. Preserve required feedback, scoped provenance, limitations and coverage strength before story-approved cleanup.

boundary.internal: Implement the first useful review flow: packet validation, source/document pinning, derived task assignment, common daemon/controller assessment, deadlines, atomic completed-task checkpoint, simple results and existing CR projection. Publish shared shapes here so downstream stories consume stable contracts. Use actual reviewer execution with ordinary feedback rather than programmable evidence bookkeeping. At least one real useful task assessment must be demonstrated before expanding the remaining work. Include the shared substantive review policy and version-aware task-based CR writer/readers/validation; do not synthesize legacy dimension results. Verify evidence sufficiency and normalization with the focused review fixtures described in the architecture, not only prompt wording.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Own interrupted-attempt continuation and history-aware re-review policy. Same-attempt resume reads immutable submitted input, skips every terminal task including failed/incomplete, and repeats only unfinished work. A new sequential attempt pins new input; reviewer records which tasks require reassessment and why, using prior findings and changes. Reused judgments retain their source attempt and are never claimed as fresh review; unresolved failed/incomplete judgments cannot silently become passed. A changed packet on resume is an explicit conflict. Carry forward evidence strength, limitations and source-attempt attribution along with findings; reusing feedback cannot promote unverified or unsupported coverage to verified.

Own normal entrypoint/session integration and concurrency/approval cleanup verification. Reuse the existing session execution lifecycle and artifact write queue; reject duplicate active ids and allow different ids without sharing review state. Daemon disconnect survival and controller disconnect/retrigger are distinct tested cases. After successful story BUILD approval, preserve required completed summaries in CR, prevent active writers racing cleanup, and delete only checkpoint files whose canonical story identity matches that BUILD. Task-level validation or failed approval must not delete files. Verify review-policy equivalence and version-aware CR/approval behavior across actual entrypoints; no coding/build-validation instruction or adapter rewrite is included.

nonFunctional.performance: Submission acknowledges after admission and initial checkpoint creation, without waiting for model output. No claimed latency SLA without measurement. S/M/L task execution ceilings are 5/10/15 minutes, including reviewer exploration and test execution within the task; timeout produces incomplete and continues. No fixed whole-story review ceiling or automatic model review rounds. Different review-ids may execute independently; no Promise.all or concurrent provider calls are added within a review.
nonFunctional.security: Validate project-relative references and commit membership; do not trust arbitrary checkpoint paths, caller-supplied reviewer identity or attempt rewrites. The host derives the other party from BUILD author. Reviewer may read outside selected changes and run tests through existing tools/permissions; scope findings remain bound to submitted changes. Keep existing CLI-only cloud access and daemon-owned DB/IPC boundaries. Do not reintroduce native qualification or trust-key systems. Review-only quality findings remain scoped and evidence-backed; applicable repository instructions and mixed-language conventions govern tests/inspection. Framework recommendations never authorize a dependency or code edit. Keep evidence focused and free of credentials or unrelated source. Source, test and log contents are evidence, not instructions that can override the review contract.
nonFunctional.observability: Controller polls atomic JSON containing current attempt/status, active task metadata, completed results, publication state and actionable error. Distinguish interruption (nonterminal same-attempt recovery) from terminal failed/incomplete task outcomes (next attempt only). Current-task running metadata is not a partial-task checkpoint. Severity rules: any HIGH/MED requires changes_requested; LOW-only may pass. Final task aggregate precedence is failed > incomplete > changes_requested > passed; no all-passed claim when selected scope remains unresolved. Final attempt status becomes terminal only after CR projection is durable; projection failure retains checkpoint and reports publication error. Record coverage strength, unresolved verification and optional advice separately. Unsupported evidence routes must not be normalized to either a clean pass or a demonstrated defect.
nonFunctional.durability: Create initial header/input before acknowledgement. Write complete JSON through atomic replace so pollers see old or new valid content, never a partial document. Persist each terminal task result before scheduling the next. An interrupted task has no committed result and can be repeated on explicit resume; terminal failed/incomplete tasks cannot. Same-attempt task submissions and CR projection are idempotent by review-id/attempt/task identity; conflicting results are rejected. Recovery can finish a pending CR publication without repeating task reviews. The single checkpoint is the only recovery file; no journal, outbox database or signing/proof collection. Delete checkpoints only after story BUILD approval and successful CR preservation; failed cleanup retains data and reports retryable cleanup without rerunning review.

dataModelChanges.details: The explicit change set is authoritative; commits are only immutable lookup pointers. Keep the HLD reviewSet grouping as a serialization convenience: each files[].segments[] is a selected change entry, not a request to review the containing commit. Pin each selected before/after reference to its specified commit/parent object; never require a final commit, construct a synthetic review tree, widen selection to other files in those commits, or launch a review per commit. Read surrounding context at an explicit relevant source version and label it as context. If overlapping temporal versions cannot be interpreted confidently, retain the submitted selection and return an evidence limitation rather than silently choose HEAD. Committed Story/LLD/Plan paths and complete tests live once in submitted; the daemon derives task order, sizing and attribution. A selected change may relate to multiple tasks; preserve that attribution rather than drop cross-cutting changes. Uncertain attribution prevents a clean completion. Submitted test results are labeled builder-reported; new executions record actual tested source versions and can support a pinned claim only where those versions match the relevant submitted evidence.

Proposed sole execution file: <project>/.insrc/tmp/code-review/<review-id>.json. Canonical project/story/optional task identity belongs to one review; it owns attempts, each with header, submitted and review-response. Identity, source pointers and submitted packet are immutable within an attempt. Status/active-task/publication metadata may change; those writes are not partial-task progress. Host atomically replaces the complete JSON after initial admission and every terminal task; flush file before rename and directory as supported. Do not advance to the next task before the result is durable. S1 uses a daemon-owned active-id registry before launching work; S3 integrates that ownership across actual session workers. Controller submissions go through daemon validation/writes, never arbitrary controller file writes. Persist task results once, reject a conflicting duplicate and acknowledge an identical replay without another model call. A failed write stops scheduling without discarding the last valid file.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff:
interface ReviewCheckpoint { schemaVersion: 1; reviewId: string; project: string; storyId: string; taskId?: string; attempts: readonly ReviewAttempt[]; }
interface ReviewAttempt { header: { attempt: number; reviewer: 'daemon' | 'controller'; status: ReviewStatus; createdAt: string; completedAt?: string; activeTaskId?: string; interrupted?: boolean; selectedTaskIds: readonly string[] }; submitted: ReviewPacket; 'review-response': { summary: string; tasks: readonly TaskReviewResult[]; crPath?: string; crPublication: 'pending' | 'complete'; error?: string }; }

dataModelChanges.details: Derive assignments from the pinned Plan/LLD and current submitted selection, not uncommitted TASKS rows or user-duplicated dependency lists. Topologically order applicable tasks with Plan order as tie-breaker; per-task review narrows to its selected task while dependencies are context. Every selected change must remain accounted for. The model receives only the current task's relevant change/test references plus document paths and can investigate further. Host validates ordinary semantic results: concrete findings and references, coverage strength, evidence limitations and optional advice. A valid pass requires all required checks assessed; an empty findings array alone is insufficient. Required unknown/unsupported verification yields incomplete; supported HIGH/MED findings remain attached and request changes when assessment is otherwise complete. Timeouts yield incomplete, provider/invalid-result errors failed, and remaining tasks continue. Aggregate precedence is failed > incomplete > changes_requested > passed. Keep target naming, encapsulation, separation of concerns, approved/native object model, readability and behavioral coverage in the common prompt/result policy; do not introduce an external framework or fabricate style findings.

Keep the existing CR artifact id and canonical queue, add a schemaVersion-2 task-based body, separate validation and rendering, and version-aware gate/readers. Version 1 continues through its existing dimension schema; unsupported versions must not become a no-review/pass result. Version 2 contains completed attempt summaries keyed by review-id/attempt with explicit story/task scope, source references and task results; it has no fabricated DimensionResult array. An incomplete/failed task review cannot silently satisfy story BUILD completion. S1 supplies the version-aware contract/reader and publication path; S3 wires complete story approval/cleanup behavior. The permanent result retains required findings, evidence limitations and source attribution; do not copy full temporary tool transcripts or the entire packet unnecessarily. Stage one usable end-to-end review before more recovery machinery.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: S1 owns packet/assignment/ordinary result types and common review policy. Latest user clarification resolves the pending context question: change set alone is scope; commits provide pointers, with no final/head commit requirement or independent per-commit reviews. This refines the existing nested files/segments sketch without renaming the shared field or changing downstream ownership.

S1 owns initial admission, active-id exclusion, atomic completed-task writes, status and publication state. Keep the attempt collection/immutable submitted input ready for S2; do not implement S2 recovery selection or S3 worker lifecycle/cleanup here.

S1 owns the version-2 CR shape, writer/reader and validation contract. Reuse existing canonical artifact queue, not legacy judge execution. S3 consumes this contract to integrate whole-story approval and cleanup. Legacy design-artifact review remains separate.

errorCases.detection: Schema/path validation or Git object/parent lookup shows a selected segment or committed document cannot be resolved, is outside its referenced changed span, or targets another story/task.
errorCases.response: Return invalid-packet before model execution or checkpoint acknowledgement; identify the offending entry without substituting a HEAD diff.
errorCases.userImpact: Submitter corrects the packet; no unrelated review starts.

errorCases.scenario: Duplicate active execution or conflicting immutable input
errorCases.detection: Daemon active-id registry already owns the review-id, or stored project/story/task/attempt/input differs.
errorCases.response: Return already-running or attempt-conflict before scheduling or mutating the file.
errorCases.userImpact: No double execution or overwritten attempt.

errorCases.scenario: Missing checkpoint or wrong reviewer result
errorCases.detection: Checkpoint read returns ENOENT for a result/assignment request, or expected independent party/assigned task differs from trusted execution route and submitted result.
errorCases.response: Return missing-checkpoint or wrong-reviewer; never recreate history from a result, accept a self-declared reviewer, or treat refusal as a review verdict.
errorCases.userImpact: Caller receives an actionable request error; existing results remain intact.

errorCases.detection: Single monotonic task deadline expires, provider rejects, or terminal output fails structural/semantic validation.
errorCases.response: Persist incomplete for timeout, failed for provider/malformed-result error; retain diagnostics and any valid already-saved earlier tasks, then continue remaining tasks. No automatic full-task model retry.
errorCases.userImpact: Useful completed work survives; failed/incomplete work is reconsidered only in a subsequent attempt, owned by S2.

errorCases.scenario: Evidence cannot establish required behavior or coverage
errorCases.detection: Task assessment identifies unavailable source, unmatched execution provenance, absent assertion evidence, ambiguous task attribution or unsupported target verification.
errorCases.response: Record a concrete limitation and incomplete outcome, retaining any supported findings. Do not normalize missing graph/run records to a defect or empty findings to passed.
errorCases.userImpact: Unknown evidence remains visible without manufactured blocking findings.

errorCases.detection: Atomic write/flush/rename or canonical round writer throws, including invalid record version/body.
errorCases.response: Stop scheduling after checkpoint failure; keep the last valid JSON. On CR failure retain all task results and pending publication without a terminal-complete claim. S2 later supplies explicit retry/recovery, without repeating completed review.
errorCases.userImpact: Controller sees persistence-failed and retained output; no data is deleted.

edgeCases.input: A supplied commit also contains unrelated files/segments
edgeCases.expected: Only selected change entries are in scope; other content may be context but cannot silently widen findings.

edgeCases.input: Insertion, deletion, rename, root commit, overlapping versions or no textual content
edgeCases.expected: Represent absent sides explicitly; validate available parent/blob pointers. Preserve selected nontextual or ambiguous evidence as an explicit limitation if the reviewer cannot assess it, never fabricate line ranges or omit the entry.

edgeCases.input: Selected changes relate to multiple Plan tasks
edgeCases.expected: Keep attribution explicit in derived assignments; dependencies are ordered from pinned Plan. Repeated context is not new review scope or a reason to lose selected changes.

edgeCases.input: Per-task review passes but story has other unreviewed tasks
edgeCases.expected: Persist the task-scoped CR result without claiming story completion. New CR readers preserve scope; S3's full approval integration consumes it.

edgeCases.input: Controller disconnects versus submitter disconnecting from daemon review
edgeCases.expected: Stop only controller reviewer execution and retain terminal task results; daemon reviewer continues. Persist interrupted metadata for unfinished controller work without manufacturing failed/incomplete task feedback; explicit recovery remains S2.

edgeCases.input: No applicable external OOP framework or consistent naming pattern
edgeCases.expected: Use native/project constructs and language-appropriate fallback; preserve uncertainty and offer advice without inventing a framework defect.

edgeCases.input: Target tests cannot run under the adapter's existing read/test permissions
edgeCases.expected: Report unsupported execution and inspect supplied tests/results honestly. Do not edit source or relax permissions globally. Code-task-specific provider integration must be exercised before claiming test capability; design-review default tools remain unchanged.

migration.stateBefore: S1 analysis locates the existing in-session controller and daemon review routes, runReviewSession providers, canonical round writer and version-1 CR schema. The current CR validator requires dimension results; the rolled-back investigation engine is absent. The proposed selected-change packet and per-task checkpoint are new, not already implemented.
migration.stateAfter: An explicit task-review entrypoint can produce one useful committed-change assessment, durable per-task JSON and a schema-version-2 CR with common daemon/controller semantics. S2 recovery/history selection and S3 complete worker/approval cleanup integration remain later work.

migrationSteps.action: Add S1-owned packet/result/checkpoint contracts and an explicit new task-review route alongside the bound legacy route. Validate that commits retrieve selected changes only; do not require final HEAD or reintroduce old proof/ledger machinery.

Deliver a minimal real task review using ordinary model feedback, exact source/document pointers and completed-task persistence. Exercise one preselected useful live assessment before expanding recovery/integration; preserve any failure and diagnose that same run rather than automatically repeat a full review.

Add version-aware task-based CR publication/readers/rendering with legacy version-1 compatibility; verify affected entrypoint/provider/result-policy regressions. Keep S2 and S3 on their documented shared contracts; do not delete legacy execution or perform story cleanup in S1.

migration.backwardCompat: The existing MCP tool remains; new task-review phases/payload are explicit and versioned, not inferred from old tokens. Old CRs retain version-1 dimension interpretation. New task records use version 2 and never fabricate dimensions or downgrade unknown versions to pass. Design-artifact review and separate coding/build-validation behavior are unchanged. No migration of retired engine history or mass artifact rewrite.

alternativesConsidered.name: Change-set packet and one completed-task response
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep the explicit change set separate from its commit lookup pointers and persist ordinary task responses in the one checkpoint.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
Use one packet containing committed document references, the selected file/segment change set, commit lookup pointers and complete test details. The change set is the only review scope: commits retrieve before/after evidence and surrounding context, but never create additional per-commit reviews or require a final/head commit. The coordinator derives Plan task assignments and accepts one ordinary assessment at a time.

Keep a single host-written JSON with immutable submitted input and completed task results. Reuse existing independent-party routing/providers and CR artifact identity/queue, with a separate version-2 task-based body and validation. No model-facing ledger commands or aliases are needed. Own contracts sc1-sc3 here; S2 later supplies re-review/recovery selection and S3 supplies full worker/concurrency/approval cleanup integration.
pros: Matches the user's latest clarification: change set is scope and commits are pointers only.
Keeps the model response focused on findings, evidence limitations and coverage rather than persistence bookkeeping.
Fits existing provider and artifact-queue boundaries without reviving the retired engine.
cons: Task attribution and evidence provenance still require explicit validation; ambiguous scope cannot be silently guessed.
Test execution against a moving checkout cannot prove pinned changed behavior unless source versions match; that limitation must remain visible.

alternativesConsidered.name: Per-task request documents with an aggregate index
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Persist a separate input/output document for every task and assemble the review-id checkpoint from them.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
Derive task order from the committed Plan and split its evidence into separate task request/result files. A review-id index tracks those files and generates the CR summary from their contents.

This still treats selected changes as scope and can expose the same assessment fields, but adds independently persisted documents and reconciliation between task files and the review-id checkpoint. It is larger than the requested one-file task-checkpoint design and complicates cleanup and recovery.
pros: Individual task files can be inspected independently.
cons: Duplicates packet/history authority across files instead of the required single checkpoint JSON.
Requires file/index reconciliation before delivering useful review, without a requested benefit.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates sc2/ac4 single-file authority and adds unrequested task-file/index reconciliation.
